content_html:
Hiking at altitudes above 4,000 meters is an incredible experience, but it requires physical and mental preparation to avoid altitude sickness and enjoy it to the fullest. Here are some key tips to get ready.

1. Pre-workout: Improve your endurance and strength

Before facing a high-altitude hike, it is essential to prepare your body with exercises that improve your cardiovascular endurance and strengthen your muscles:

  • Cardio: Run, brisk walk, bike ride, or climb stairs to strengthen your heart and lungs.
  • Leg training: Do squats, lunges, and balance exercises to strengthen your legs and joints.
  • Weighted walks: Hike with a loaded backpack to get used to the extra effort.

2. Acclimatization: The key to avoiding altitude sickness

Acute mountain sickness (soroche) is common when you quickly climb above 2,500 meters. To minimize it:

  • Gradually ascend: If possible, spend a few days at intermediate altitudes before the hike.
  • Hydrate yourself well: Drink at least 3 liters of water a day to help your body adapt.
  • Avoid alcohol and tobacco: They can dehydrate you and affect your oxygenation.
  • Take coca or muña infusion: They are natural remedies used in the Andes to improve adaptation.

3. Food for altitude

Your diet should be balanced and rich in carbohydrates, since at altitude the body burns more energy:

  • Eat complex carbohydrates: Quinoa, potatoes, rice and bread will give you sustained energy.
  • Includes lean proteins: Chicken, fish and legumes help muscle recovery.
  • Avoid heavy meals: Digestion is slower at altitude, opt for moderate portions.

4. Proper equipment

The correct clothing and equipment will make your hike more comfortable and safe:

  • Layered clothing: A thermal jacket, a windproof coat and a raincoat will protect you from changes in temperature.
  • Suitable footwear: Wear comfortable trekking boots with good traction.
  • Sun protection: At higher altitudes, UV rays are stronger. Wear sunscreen, sunglasses and a hat.

You can buy all of this in Cusco itself, more information here.
